60.0.0.en: 1 "Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the LORD is risen upon thee. 2 For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but the LORD shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.

60.0.1.en: The Lord had already affirmed that He Himself accomplishes the salvation and redeems Zion, establishing His new covenant with her (Isa 59:15-21). Now that the Lord Christ has offered His salvation on the Cross, and the Father has declared His acceptance through the Resurrection -which is not a gift external to the Lord Christ, since He Himself is the Resurrection (Jn 11:25), and He has power to lay down His life and power to take it again (Jn 10:18)- He asks the Church of the New Testament to enjoy the life of her Redeemer as a risen life in which there is no place for darkness.

60.1.0.en: "Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the LORD is risen upon thee. For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but the LORD shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee" [2].

60.1.1.en: When the Jews returned from captivity they counted themselves as those who had risen from the dead, and they enjoyed the light of life and freedom after seventy years of humiliation as in the darkness of the tomb. But the Church of the New Testament has enjoyed something greater: her union with the true Light as an eternal Bridegroom, who makes of her a bride bearing His light, His splendor and His glory. As the Lord said of Himself, "I am the light of the world" (Jn 8:12), He called His disciples the light of the world (Mt 5:14), since they bear Him within them.

60.1.2.en: What is the secret of the Church's illumination?

60.1.3.en: The Lord's Resurrection, which gave us the new life that death will not overcome, that darkness cannot seize, and that the tomb cannot destroy. Therefore the Apostle says: "Awake thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall give thee light" (Eph 5:14).

60.1.4.en: Since Baptism is the enjoyment of Christ's Resurrection in us, this sacrament was called "illumination".

60.1.5.en: * When we are baptized we are enlightened, when we are enlightened we are adopted as sons, when we are adopted we are made perfect...

60.1.6.en: This act is called by many names, I mean grace, illumination, perfection, washing... It is illumination because by it we see the holy light of salvation, I mean that by it we gaze upon God clearly.

60.1.7.en: St. Clement of Alexandria * Illumination, which is Baptism... is the helper of the weak... a sharing in light... a shaking off of darkness.

60.1.8.en: Illumination is a vessel sailing toward God; a keeping company with Christ, the foundation of religion, the perfection of the mind!

60.1.9.en: Illumination is the key of the Kingdom and the restoration of life.

60.1.10.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus * Baptism is the daughter of the day; it opened its doors and the night, into which all creation had entered, fled!

60.1.11.en: Mar Jacob of Serugh Thus, when we accept union with our Lord Jesus Christ the Crucified, we are buried with Him in Baptism and rise bearing the possibility of new life, to live as is fitting, as children of light and members of the body of the holy Christ. It is not fitting for us to descend again into the darkness of sin, nor to excuse ourselves by our human weakness, for we bear within us the light of the Lord and His glory shines upon us. We no longer become a dark earth but a heaven that embraces the glory and splendor of God.

60.1.12.en: This is the mark of the Church as a new life in Christ, who dwells in her and shines upon her with His divine righteousness, so that it is said of us: "Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven" (Mt 5:16).

60.1.13.en: * When they practice divine things and speak of them, and live the divine life, overcoming hardness of heart and enjoying the peace of righteousness, a great glory pursues them in the Church of Christ.

60.1.14.en: St. Augustine Since the Lord Christ came into the world to win humanity as a bride for Himself, He pours His glory and splendor within her; He gives her His Holy Spirit to adorn her and beautify her, so that she may be prepared with inner glory for the eternal heavenly wedding. So it is said to her: "Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear; forget also thine own people, and thy father's house; so shall the king greatly desire thy beauty: for he is thy Lord; and worship thou him... The king's daughter is all glorious within" (Ps 45:10-13).

60.2.0.en: 3 "And the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising. 4 Lift up thine eyes round about, and see: all they gather themselves together, they come to thee: thy sons shall come from far, and thy daughters shall be nursed at thy side. 5 Then thou shalt see, and flow together, and thine heart shall fear, and be enlarged; because the abundance of the sea shall be converted unto thee, the forces of the Gentiles shall come unto thee. 6 The multitude of camels shall cover thee, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah; all they from Sheba shall come: they shall bring gold and incense; and they shall shew forth the praises of the LORD. 7 All the flocks of Kedar shall be gathered together unto thee, the rams of Nebaioth shall minister unto thee: they shall come up with acceptance on mine altar, and I will glorify the house of my glory. 8 Who are these that fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their windows? 9 Surely the isles shall wait for me, and the ships of Tarshish first, to bring thy sons from far, their silver and their gold with them, unto the name of the LORD thy God, and to the Holy One of Israel, because he hath glorified thee.

60.2.1.en: The inner glory of God in the soul is attractive; it wins souls for His spiritual kingdom. For the Church of the New Testament becomes an illuminated city that attracts the Gentiles, as the Lord Himself says: "Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid. Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house. Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven" (Mt 5:14-16). This is the fulfillment of what is written in the prophet Isaiah: "And the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising" [3].

60.2.2.en: The Church, like her Bridegroom, becomes a pillar of the light of truth that leads the Gentiles in the way of the Lord and sets up among them spiritual kings who have inner authority.

60.3.0.en: The Church looks around her to see on every side the wonderful work of God, who draws from all nations sons and daughters for her, coming from far to become the honored household of the Lord, carried in arms [14].

60.3.1.en: The power of Christ risen from the dead appears in the life of His Church by converting powers (the wealth of the Gentiles) for the sake of His Kingdom, for it is said to His bride: "Then thou shalt see, and flow together, and thine heart shall fear, and be enlarged; because the abundance of the sea shall be converted unto thee, the forces of the Gentiles shall come unto thee" [5]...

60.3.2.en: What is the wealth or riches of the Gentiles that are sanctified for the sake of the Church of Christ?

60.3.3.en: a. The abundance of the sea [5], that is, fish and pearls. The Fathers of the early Church counted the Lord Christ as "the Fish" (Ichthys, ἰχθύς), and the believers as the fish that live with the Lord Christ and in Him (Ezek 47:9). Tertullian says: [We little fish, after the example of our Fish, Jesus Christ, are born in water, and we are not safe in any other way than by remaining in the water continually].

60.3.4.en: b. Gold and incense carried by camels from Midian and Sheba, not for trade but offered as a gift to Zion. As the Magi offered gold, frankincense and myrrh to the Lord Christ as a sign of His kingship, that He is God to whom incense is offered, and that He suffers; so the members of His body become kings who offer incense as a sweet fragrance to the Savior.

60.3.5.en: c. The offering of acceptable sacrifices for the service of the house of the Lord and its adornment [7-8]; these sacrifices are our lives, our bodies and all our powers, which are united with the unique Sacrifice, and so become burnt offerings of love lifted up through the Cross. The Apostle says: "I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service" (Rom 12:1). Our offerings to the Lord are our very "souls", as St. Jerome says.

60.3.6.en: d. Perhaps the most beautiful thing we offer to Zion is our enjoyment of the ability to fly like a cloud, carried by the Spirit of the Lord toward the heavenly things, so that we live with our Christ in His glories as in our own home. "Who are these that fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their windows?!" [8].

60.3.7.en: The Lord will come on the last day in the clouds (Mt 24:30); He comes carried upon His saints, the light and luminous cloud (Isa 19:1)... Our likeness to a cloud means that we have become a throne bearing our Christ; and our likeness to doves means that we have become spiritual, because the Holy Spirit appeared at the Lord's baptism as a dove. In other words, our attachment to the Church of God makes us a throne for the Lord, bearing the fruits of His Holy Spirit.

60.3.8.en: In the Septuagint it says: "Who are these that fly as a cloud, and as doves with their young?" St. Gregory of Nyssa sees that this prophetic phrase announces from afar the Church coming with her children, full of beauty and very many.

60.3.9.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa compares the true children of the Church, who in lightness of spirit fly like doves and clouds, with the wicked, who because of the weight of sin sink as in deep waters. [One walks lightly enough while the other sinks in deep waters. For virtue is light and floats, and all who live in its way fly like a cloud and like doves with their young, as Isaiah says; but sin is heavy; and as another prophet says, it sits upon a talent of lead (Zech 5:7)].

60.3.10.en: e. Silver with gold [9]. If silver points to the word of God (Ps 12:6), then gold points to the pure heavenly life; so the wealth of the Church coming from the Gentiles lies in her clinging to the word of God and her enjoyment of the heavenly mind.

60.4.0.en: 10 "And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee. 11 Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought. 12 For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted. 13 The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious. 14 The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; and all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet; and they shall call thee, The city of the LORD, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel. 15 Whereas thou hast been forsaken and hated, so that no man went through thee, I will make thee an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations. 16 Thou shalt also suck the milk of the Gentiles, and shalt suck the breast of kings: and thou shalt know that I the LORD am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob. 17 For brass I will bring gold, and for iron I will bring silver, and for wood brass, and for stones iron: I will also make thy officers peace, and thine exactors righteousness. 18 Violence shall no more be heard in thy land, wasting nor destruction within thy borders; but thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise. 19 The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the LORD shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory. 20 Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself: for the LORD shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended. 21 Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified. 22 A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation: I the LORD will hasten it in his time."

60.4.1.en: a. "And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee" [10]. Here he points to Cyrus, the stranger by race, who ordered the return of the captives, and to the facilities given to Nehemiah to build the wall.

60.4.2.en: God in His love uses all foreign powers for the building of His Kingdom, offering every good for the sake of His Church; and this is the true glory of the Church: the sanctifying of every work!

60.5.0.en: b. The beauty of the Church is poured out in the opening of her gates continually, "they shall not be shut day nor night" [11]. She does not turn away a sinner nor wound his feelings; she bears a heart enlarged with love, like her Bridegroom, toward all.

60.6.0.en: She is like Noah's ark, whose doors were wide, receiving Noah and his family and the animals and birds, etc... Whoever was inside was saved, but whoever refused perished. "For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted" [12]. As the martyr Cyprian says: [There is no salvation outside the Church].

60.7.0.en: c. "The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious" [13]. Lebanon was known for its excellent trees, so its wealth of timber is turned to the adornment of the temple of the Lord. A wonderful picture of converting idle powers, or those that have been misused, for the sake of the temple of the Lord.

60.8.0.en: d. Enjoying spiritual authority, where the powers of darkness are subjected under the feet of the believers. "The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; and all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet; and they shall call thee, The city of the LORD, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel" [14]. Even the enemy of good, with all his powers, bears witness to the believers that they are the holy city of God. The wicked cannot but testify to the children of God of the holiness of their lives, even in the moments of their persecuting them.

60.9.0.en: e. Her enjoyment of everlasting joy: "Whereas thou hast been forsaken and hated, so that no man went through thee, I will make thee an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations" [15]. This is her eternal pride, that she is no longer forsaken and no longer suffers a state of emptiness or isolation or the hatred of others toward her, but is filled with joy and becomes glorious forever.

60.9.1.en: f. God gives her more than she asks and above what she requests: if she asks for brass He gives her gold, and if she asks for iron He gives her silver, and instead of wood He offers her brass, and in place of stones iron... Thus she finds in God her inner satisfaction, and also the secret of her spiritual wealth and the satisfaction of all her needs.

60.10.0.en: g. Justice dwells in her, therefore "Violence shall no more be heard in thy land, wasting nor destruction within thy borders; but thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise" [18]. Every man finds in her his salvation and the secret of his praise and joy, because the just God in her grants justice and righteousness, and does not permit injustice or destruction or oppression to be practiced within her.

60.11.0.en: h. As the icon of heaven she needs no sun or moon to light her, "but the LORD shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory" [19].

60.13.0.en: j. Enjoying the surpassing power of God: "A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation" [22]. Man in himself is counted small, but as a member of the body of Christ he is counted a thousand, that is, heavenly, because the number 1000 points to heaven. Outside Christ he is counted despised, played with by the enemy of good and crushed by sin, but in Christ Jesus he becomes a strong nation. He becomes a "nation" when he bears holy powers of spirit and body working together in harmony and unity, bearing within them the power of the Spirit of the Lord.

60.13.1.en: Thus this chapter presents to us a living picture of the Church of the Lord Christ as the illuminated city bearing within her the radiance of the Lord Christ, attracting the Gentiles and peoples through her inner glory, and sanctifying all their powers and abilities that they had misused. She opens her gates before all with love, and the Lord opens His gates before her to give her more than she asks and above what she requests; He gives her His righteousness, His justice, His power, His beauty and His light, so that nothing is lacking to her!
